def read_skill(name: str) -> str:  [sync]

def tool_a() -> dict:  [sync]
    Fetch current CPU load (independent — no inputs needed).
    
    Returns:
        load       (float) — CPU load 0.0–1.0. Changes every call.
        status     (str)   — "high" if load > 0.7, else "normal".

def tool_b() -> dict:  [sync]
    Fetch available memory stats (independent — no inputs needed).
    
    Returns:
        available_mb (int) — Available memory in MB. Changes every call.
        total_mb     (int) — Total memory in MB.
        pct_free     (float) — Fraction free 0.0–1.0.

def tool_c(load: float, available_mb: int, total_mb: int) -> dict:  [sync]
    Decide if a job can run now — depends on BOTH tool_a and tool_b results.
    You MUST pass the actual values returned by tool_a and tool_b — do not guess.
    
    Args:
        load         (float) — CPU load from tool_a.
        available_mb (int)   — Available MB from tool_b.
        total_mb     (int)   — Total MB from tool_b.
    
    Returns:
        can_run        (bool) — True if safe to run.
        reason         (str)  — Why.
        recommendation (str)  — What to do next.

def tool_d(can_run: bool, reason: str, recommendation: str, active_users: int, quiet_window: bool) -> dict:  [sync]
    Generate final action plan — depends on tool_c AND tool_e results.
    You MUST pass actual values from tool_c and tool_e — do not guess.
    
    Args:
        can_run      (bool) — From tool_c: whether resources allow the job.
        reason       (str)  — From tool_c: explanation of the decision.
        recommendation (str) — From tool_c: what to do about resources.
        active_users (int)  — From tool_e: current active users.
        quiet_window (bool) — From tool_e: True if low-traffic window.
    
    Returns:
        action       (str)  — "START", "SCHEDULE", or "ABORT".
        schedule_at  (str)  — When to run if not now (e.g. "off-peak window").
        explanation  (str)  — Full reasoning combining resource + user signals.
        priority     (str)  — "HIGH", "MEDIUM", or "LOW".

def tool_e() -> dict:  [sync]
    Fetch active user count on the system (independent — no inputs needed).
    
    Returns:
        active_users (int)  — Number of active users right now. Changes every call.
        peak_users   (int)  — Peak users today.
        quiet_window (bool) — True if now is a low-traffic window (safe for heavy jobs).
